asset: 2000 Nissan Altima (L30) - fully disassemblable Blender asset

coordinate_system.convention: +X = forward (nose), +Y = left side, +Z = up, Z=0 = ground
coordinate_system.origin: mid-point of the wheelbase, projected to the ground plane

sequence.order: assembly order (bottom-up); play in reverse to reassemble

steps.title: Bare engine block and lower end
steps.note: cylinder block, crankcase girdle, oil pan and block hardware

steps.title: Crankshaft and drive plate
steps.note: crankshaft and flex plate, lifted out of the block

steps.title: Pistons and connecting rods
steps.note: four piston / connecting-rod assemblies, drawn up out of the bores

steps.title: Cylinder head and gasket
steps.note: cylinder head, multi-layer steel gasket and head bolts

steps.title: Camshafts, valve cover and ignition
steps.note: both DOHC camshafts, cam bearing caps, valve cover and spark plugs

steps.title: Timing chain set and front cover
steps.note: timing chain cover, crank and cam sprockets, chain and tensioner

steps.title: Intake side and fuel injection
steps.note: intake manifold, runners, throttle body, air box and fuel rail/injectors

steps.title: Exhaust side and manifold
steps.note: exhaust manifold, runners, heat shield, upstream O2 sensor and studs

steps.title: Cooling system
steps.note: water pump, thermostat, radiator, hoses, reservoir and cooling fans

steps.title: Accessory drive
steps.note: alternator, power steering pump, A/C compressor, tensioner and belts

steps.title: Transaxle and driveline
steps.note: transaxle case, torque converter, valve body, final drive and mounts

steps.title: Engine-bay completion
steps.note: engine cover, EGR/EVAP hardware, engine mounts and remaining bay fasteners

steps.title: Remaining engine-bay hardware
steps.note: engine parts not owned by steps 01-12, plus emission control and battery

steps.title: Interior cabin trim and seating
steps.note: dashboard, seats, console, carpet, headliner, door cards and cabin trim

steps.title: Electrical harness and modules
steps.note: every routed wire segment, connector, grommet, clip, module, fuse, relay and the antenna

steps.title: Exterior body panels and moldings
steps.note: hood, trunk lid, fenders, bumper covers, grille, fuel door, moldings, badges and emblems

steps.title: Glazing, lamps and mirrors
steps.note: windscreen, backlight, quarter glass, door glass, all lamp assemblies and mirrors

steps.title: Door assemblies and seals
steps.note: the four door shells and hardware, the standalone door module parts, and all weatherstrip

steps.title: Wheels, tyres and brakes
steps.note: rims, tyres, hub caps, valve stems, lug nuts, discs, calipers, pads and hydraulic parts

steps.title: Suspension and steering
steps.note: struts, springs, control arms, knuckles, hubs, beam axle, stabiliser bars, rack and column

steps.title: Exhaust system
steps.note: manifold heat shield, downpipe, catalyst, midpipe, resonator, muffler, tailpipe and sensors

steps.title: Fluids, tanks and fuel system
steps.note: fuel tank, pump, filler neck, feed and return lines, washer reservoir, oil and power-steering fluid

steps.title: Structural fasteners
steps.note: the general bolt, washer, nut and lug-nut population across the whole car

steps.title: Clips, retainers and fixings
steps.note: trim clips, retainers, hose clamps and tie straps

steps.title: Body shell and structure
steps.note: floor, roof bows, wheel houses, strut towers, radiator support, parcel shelf, spare well, ribs, braces and shell hardware - the reference hull, so it barely moves while every other system lifts away from it

steps.title: Remaining driveline
steps.note: drive shafts, CV joints and boots, shift cable and transaxle hardware not owned by step 11

steps.title: Remaining hardware and safety systems
steps.note: safety restraints, screws and studs, and any part not claimed by an earlier step - the catch-all that makes the sequence total

wiring.description: Real, physically modelled wiring - every wire is its own selectable object with a baked trace coordinate

trace.meaning: normalised arc length along the run (0.0 start, 1.0 end)
trace.note: sweeping TraceProgress 0->1 lights the wire progressively from one end to the other

hoses.description: Real, physically modelled hoses and tie straps - every hose is a swept tube along its actual run, every strap a swept band wrapping it

trace.meaning: normalised arc length along the run (0.0 start, 1.0 end)
trace.note: hoses and straps carry the same trace shader as the wiring
